remit: X12 defines this reason as a benefit that is included in the payment or allowance for another service or procedure that has already been adjudicated. The 835 may include a Healthcare Policy Identification Segment (loop 2110, REF) pointing to the payer policy.
metaDescription: CO-97 denial explained: the payment is included in the allowance for another service. How bundling edits work, when a modifier helps, and prevention tips.
summary: The payer says this service is already included in the payment for another service billed the same day.
causes: A bundling edit treats the two services as one
A separate, distinct service was billed without the modifier that shows it
The services really are meant to be paid together
fixes: Check the payer's bundling edits for the two codes
If the services were truly separate, submit a corrected claim with the right modifier and notes that support it
If they were not, accept the bundling and adjust off the balance
prevention: Check bundling edits for common code pairs before billing
Document separate, distinct services clearly so the modifier is supportable

faqs.question: Can a modifier always override CO-97?
faqs.answer: No. A modifier helps only when the chart shows the services were truly distinct. Using one to avoid a bundling edit is a compliance risk.

faqs.question: Is CO-97 a denial?
faqs.answer: It is a reduction because the service is considered included in another payment. Whether to challenge it depends on whether the services were separate.
